Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> In Focus | National | Telecom Ghana Publishing Company forgoes 2025 dividend payment despite recording GH¢16.9m profit, opts to reinvest profits Source : Myjoyonline.com 26 November 2026 7:37pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Ghana Publishing Company Limited (GPCL) will not pay dividends to its sole shareholder for the 2025 financial year, opting instead to reinvest its profits in the modernisation of its printing equipment.
The decision comes despite the company's strong financial performance, which saw revenue increase by 20% to GH¢72.9 million and profit after tax rise to GH¢16.9 million.
Board Chairman, Mathew Lawer Teye, announced the decision at the company's Annual General Meeting on Thursday, November 26, 2026.
"After careful deliberation, the Board has decided not to recommend the payment of a dividend for the 2025 financial year, despite the strong financial performance," he stated.
Mr Teye acknowledged that the decision could disappoint the government, which is the company's sole shareholder.
"I know this will disappoint our Shareholder, and I ask for your patience. We are reinvesting most of the profit to modernise our offset printing machines. This capital investment will build the capacity that will transform our profitability," he said.
He explained that retaining the profits would help strengthen the company's operations and support its long-term financial performance.
"Every cedi we hold back today is a cedi that will help us sustain the performance of the company tomorrow," he added.
Mr Teye described the company's 2025 financial performance as exceptional, highlighting improvements in revenue and profitability.
Revenue increased by 20% to GH¢72.9 million, while profit after tax reached GH¢16.9 million, more than six times the previous year's figure.
He attributed the growth mainly to management's efforts to reduce operating costs and increase income.
Operating costs as a proportion of revenue declined from 92.3% in 2024 to 73.1% in 2025, according to the Board Chairman.
The company is expected to continue its retooling programme and digital transformation efforts as part of plans to improve operational capacity and sustain its financial performance.
